issue_context.title: Setting enumName doesn't change how migrations get generated
issue_context.body:
I want to share enum names with the same values across several tables, but after making the changes `generateMigrations` doesn't actually change anything. `enumNames` ought to also be reflected in migration generation

### Original comment in enumName PR

@ejose19 - am i'm right in thinking this won't affect the migrations generated? It appears they're still being prefixed with table names and ignoring the new `enumName`..

I can take a crack at a PR if i can get a few pointers..

_Originally posted by @elmpp in https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/pull/4824#issuecomment-545484163_
comments: an attempt at #5479 to try to see if that would fix it, would appreciate a look by someone who actually knows this repo to confirm i'm going in the right direction.

Yes you're correct. When I implemented the patch I just did the core for active operations, not the migrations. As I suggested in that thread, find the files related to migrations and make your way from here.
Using the same enum across multiple tables currently breaks migration generation, so any help with this would be greatly apprecaited.
@golergka when i get the chance i'll try to finish up that PR! hopefully later this week

@osdiab tell me if I can be of help! I use TypeORM pretty extensively, but haven't do any contribution to the library itself yet, so it seems like a problem I wouldn't be able to take on my own - but if you have any easier sub-tasks I would be glad.

@golergka me neither 😅 but I made one contribution before and I think the one I made is pretty close, just need to make the remaining tests pass. If you wanna give patching up my outstanding PR a go feel free and I’ll be happy to advise, but if not it’ll probably be later this week or early next for me.

What is the status of this?

I'm currently in the same situation that I would like to specify the full name of the enum independently from the table its being used in. When I change the name of the enum via a migration script, the next migration generation will generate a script, which renames it back.

@tbf-siteimprove my PR has been ready for a long time but just hasn't been reviewed or merged - looks like @imnotjames is starting to actively maintain typeorm now so im crossing my fingers that it'll be merged sometime.

review_comments:
Should we maybe be differentiating here between `null` and `undefined`? When the user sets the column default explicitly to `null` perhaps they would want the column generated to also explicitly specify `DEFAULT NULL`, even if that is probably unnecessary.

It is also already dealt with in places like this anyway:

https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/2fa6231e5903f2238b6714f52c90aaf2fe8e57eb/src/driver/mysql/MysqlQueryRunner.ts#L1877-L1878

This problem was also brought up somewhat in https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/pull/7229#discussion_r551287724 but now we have TypeScript 4.2 with support for the `??` operator. Maybe we could start using `?? null` when comparing all the fields to avoid these situations?

Now that I think about it more it might actually make sense to have such a mapping in `normalizeDefault` but I think it should be `if (defaultValue === undefined) return null` rather than vice-versa. It's a small change but I think it might save some headaches in a few months when someone else is looking at it: it makes more sense that we are saying "if the column default wasn't defined, we default to `null`" rather than "if the column was explicitly set to `null` we change it back to not being defined (and then assume that elsewhere the code will treat `undefined` as `null`)".
